claims.title: Finite scalar-linear sink-rank recovery criterion
claims.scope: one finite directed acyclic unit-capacity network over a declared prime field with one h-symbol source and scalar linear local edge operations
assumptions: every edge carries one symbol from the declared prime field
every non-source outgoing edge is a linear combination of that node's incoming edge symbols
the sink must recover every source symbol exactly with zero error
nonclaims: the result does not cover nonlinear, noisy, vector, cyclic, or interactive codes without a new derivation
field symbols and ranks are not parent-substrate hardware costs

claims.title: Per-sink multicast cut necessity
claims.scope: exact recovery of h source symbols by one sink in the declared finite scalar-linear unit-edge model
assumptions: all information reaching the sink is propagated through the declared directed edges
one cut edge carries at most one field symbol per use
nonclaims: per-sink cut adequacy is not claimed sufficient for routing-only simultaneous multicast
the repository does not promote this bounded proof into a parent-spacetime signaling theorem

claims.title: Predictive-class finite-field multicast bridge
claims.scope: a finite deterministic future-query family with K exact predictive classes and an exact h-symbol multicast code over F_p satisfying K at most p^h
assumptions: records in one predictive class have identical complete future-query signatures
distinct predictive classes are injected into distinct source vectors
every sink exactly recovers the complete source vector
nonclaims: the field-vector label need not equal the original record representation
multicasting a predictive class does not multicast an unspecified microscopic state

claims.title: Declared butterfly routing-only impossibility
claims.scope: the repository's named binary two-symbol butterfly DAG under the declared zero-or-copy routing-only scalar semantics
assumptions: source outgoing routing packets are zero or one unchanged source basis packet
intermediate outgoing routing packets are zero or one unchanged incoming packet
both sinks must recover both source symbols exactly
nonclaims: routing is not claimed inferior on every network or under every packet model
the proof does not address vector routing, time expansion, nonlinear operations, or additional side information

claims.title: Binary scalar-linear butterfly multicast solution
claims.scope: the declared butterfly network over F_2 with source symbols x_1 and x_2
assumptions: node c may transmit the linear combination x_1 plus x_2 through the shared bottleneck
each sink receives its declared direct side-information packet and the shared coded packet
nonclaims: one successful finite code is not a proof of the general multicast coding theorem
the code is exact, scalar, binary, acyclic, and common-demand

claims.title: Exhaustive binary butterfly routing separation certificate
claims.scope: all 4096 local binary scalar coefficient assignments in the declared two-symbol butterfly network
assumptions: the assignment domain is exactly the finite local coefficient product enumerated by the checker
routing-only validity uses the repository's zero-or-unchanged-copy predicate
the configured search limit exceeds the complete assignment count
nonclaims: a capped incomplete search is not reported as an impossibility result
the finite search does not rule out models outside the declared assignment space

claims.title: Exact finite-field decoder and predictive-label certificate
claims.scope: bounded prime-field matrices, declared finite DAGs, finite predictive class maps, and exact modular decoder equations
assumptions: all field operations are performed modulo the declared prime
the supplied network and local coefficient map pass structural validation
nonclaims: bounded exact checks supplement rather than replace the universal linear-algebra derivations
an injective field label convention is not a physical ontology for hidden records
